policy: Machine-readable connectivity layer for the governed data-tools.json catalog plus the two harness-native pull surfaces (WebSearch/WebFetch). Every id here MUST resolve to a walteur-kit/data-tools.json tools[].id, except the harness-native entries which have no catalog row by design (they are built into the session, not an installable package). No server.env_keys entry may ever carry a literal secret VALUE — names only. A build may only use a server whose allowed_build_classes includes its own build_class; data-pull-required-gate and data-acquisition-gate consume this allowlist at ship time.

governance.notes: MCP client + hosted API are MIT; core engine is AGPL-3.0 (do not self-host/vendor the core into WALTEUR code). Respects robots.txt by default. Hosted API sends target URLs+content to a third party — PII/DPA consideration for regulated data. Mirrors data-tools.json:14-29.

servers.pinned_version: unpinned-latest (npx -y resolves at call time; pin via package-lock if vendored)

governance.notes: Apache-2.0, commercial-safe. Does NOT enforce robots.txt by default — must run robots-respecting, stealth OFF, per-domain allowlist + rate-limit. Stealth/undetected-Chrome mode is high-risk if enabled — treat as signoff-gated separately. Mirrors data-tools.json:31-46.

servers.pinned_version: self-hosted Docker image; pin the image tag at deploy time

governance.notes: MIT, commercial-safe, normalizer only (no crawling — robots/ToS risk is on the supplied URL, not here). OCR/transcription can surface PII in output — apply redaction downstream. Optional Azure backend is OFF by default (would transmit content to Azure; DPA/residency review if enabled). Mirrors data-tools.json:48-63.

servers.pinned_version: unpinned (pip install markitdown-mcp; pin exact version in lockfile if vendored)

governance.notes: BSD-3-Clause, commercial-safe. No first-party MCP server (community wrappers are unvetted — do not use). Must set ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True (library default is False) and an identifying User-Agent. Mirrors data-tools.json:65-80.

MIT license clean; USAGE is the exposure. Impersonates a human, can bypass login walls, robots NOT honored by default. Owned/authorized targets only; stealth/proxy/CAPTCHA OFF without legal sign-off. Mirrors data-tools.json:82-96 (risk=high).

Apache-2.0 license clean. No first-party MCP server (Apify platform MCP exposes Crawlee-based Actors separately — treat as a distinct id if adopted). Fingerprint spoofing + residential-proxy rotation defeat bot defenses — disable by policy; Apify proxy adds a third-party data-processor (DPA/GDPR review). Mirrors data-tools.json:99-113 (risk=high).

MIT license clean; entire value is misrepresenting client identity to defeat bot detection — frequently violates ToS, may implicate anti-circumvention/CFAA. Mandatory domain allowlist + robots/ToS pre-check + rate-limit + PII redaction + per-source legal sign-off. No MCP server. Mirrors data-tools.json:116-130 (risk=high).

MIT, commercial-safe. Parser only (BeautifulSoup wrapper, not a fetcher) — robots/ToS risk is on the paired fetcher, not here. No MCP server; pair with curl_cffi or firecrawl as transport. Mirrors data-tools.json:133-147.

Built into the Claude Code session; not an installable package and has no data-tools.json row by design (harness-native exemption). No liveness probe applies — session-availability is the only precondition and it cannot be exec/HTTP probed from outside the session.
